# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_CONTRACTION_BREAKOUT_SHORT

**Filed:** 2026-07-21
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

A contracted EMA ribbon (8-13-21) signals low volatility and equilibrium. A break below the ribbon with expanding volume indicates the start of a bearish move, providing a short opportunity. This captures edge by entering short after volatility contraction and before expansion, aligning with the mean-reversion to trend shift.

## Mechanism

Calculate the 8, 13, and 21-period EMAs on the 5‑minute chart. Compute ribbon width = (highest EMA - lowest EMA) / close. When ribbon width is below its 20‑period average AND price closes below the lowest EMA AND volume > 1.5× the 20‑bar average volume, enter short at the close. Exit: stop at the highest EMA or recent swing high (whichever is higher); TP1 at 2× ATR below entry; runner trails 12% off the high‑water mark. Only trade after the first 30 minutes of RTH to avoid opening noise, and only when VIX is between 12 and 22 to avoid extremely low or high volatility regimes.
